newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cargill Australia oilseeds plant on track.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cargill Australia oilseeds plant on track.

text.p: The Australian arm of privately-owned U.S. commodities trader Cargill Inc expects to bring Australia's biggest oilseeds crushing plant into production next March, company officials said on Thursday.
The A$30 million plant, under construction at Newcastle in the state of New South Wales (NSW), will produce at a rated capacity of 220,000 to 230,000 tonnes a year, mainly of canola and soybean oil.
When the Newcastle plant comes into operation, Cargill Australia Ltd would have five of the six major operating plants in Australia, officials said.
Cargill presently has oilseed crushing plants in Brisbane, Melbourne and two in western NSW, sharing the Australian market with a range of smaller competitors.
A large chunk of the oil would be for Australia's domestic market, but the company hoped to also export, they said.

The Australian move is part of a US$1.5 billion investment drive by Cargill Inc in grains and oilseeds in Asia, with the focus on oilseeds processing. India, China and Indonesia are other major investment targets.
This forms part of a push by the group to promote manufacturing past trading as the main contributor to earnings from Asia, Cargill has stated in the past.
The impact of the new plant on the Australian market would be lessened by the shutdown of a competitor's plant in Sydney in recent years, officials said.
But the Newcastle plant would strengthen Cargill's commanding share of the oilseeds action in Australia, they said.
